subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: What should OpenClaw do when a tool-capable turn returns only a bare marker like `[tool: exec]` without executable arguments?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the repair is a compatibility-sensitive provider/runtime policy choice rather than a safe mechanical parser change.

options.title: Warn and recover without executing
options.body: Detect bare markers, surface a clear diagnostic, then retry or fall back only under a maintainer-approved tool-capable policy; do not synthesize arguments.

options.title: Sanitize only
options.body: Hide or warn on the marker and leave the user to retry, which avoids unsafe execution but keeps some sessions stuck.

options.title: Provider-specific opt-in
options.body: Require affected providers or models to opt into special prompting/tool-choice behavior after live proof, leaving default behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: Warn and recover without executing
recommendation.body: Detect bare markers, surface a clear diagnostic, then retry or fall back only under a maintainer-approved tool-capable policy; do not synthesize arguments.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision is closest to the fake-tool diagnostics and runtime policy boundary he recently touched.
